answer: Behavioral cluster matching. After the fact, the system groups identities by shared timing, phrasing habits, and transaction routing patterns, treating dense clusters as one actor. Enforcement flags a whole garden of linked ids together, so faking independence requires varied timing and separate infrastructure. An attacker must pay the full cost of distinct hosting, latency jitter, and content generation per identity; one slip, like a repeated phrase or gale of synchronized joins, collapses the pearl of separate accounts into one flagged cluster.
